title: Solving two sum with a hash table
summary: Store visited elements and their indices in a hash table, checking for the complement before deciding whether to insert the current element.
context: The input consists of the integer array nums = [2, 7, 11, 15] (indexed from 0 to 3) and the target sum target = 13.

Use an auxiliary hash table map to record visited elements: each key (labeled “Element”) stores an array element value, and each value (labeled “Index”) stores that element's array index. In a single loop, each round first checks whether the complement target - nums[i] is already in map: if so, it immediately returns [map[target - nums[i]], i]; otherwise, it writes the current key-value pair nums[i]: i into map.
description: Querying the complement before inserting the current element in each round guarantees that any matched partner comes from a distinct index earlier than i. Three step-by-step frames show the check and hash-table state at i = 0, 1, and 2 in turn (note that the Step 1 frame shows the state after completing the first insertion 2: 0, rather than an empty table).
result: Assuming O(1) average-case hash lookup, the overall average time complexity is O(n) with O(n) auxiliary space, trading space for time.

frames.title: Complement 11 not found, record 2
frames.explanation: i = 0 points to element 2. As noted on the right of the figure, because 13 - 2 = 11 is not in the initially empty table, write 2: 0; now map = {2: 0}. No answer is returned yet, and the next item is 7 at index 1.
frames.key_state: i = 0 (value 2): complement 11 misses; after insertion, map = {2: 0}.
frames.announcement: Visit element 2 at index 0; complement 11 is not in the hash table, so store key-value pair 2: 0 in map.

frames.title: Complement 6 not found, record 7
frames.explanation: i = 1 points to element 7. As noted on the right of the figure, because 13 - 7 = 6 is not in map, write 7: 1. Previously the table held only key 2, and after insertion map = {2: 0, 7: 1}; no answer is returned yet, and the next item is 11 at index 2.
frames.key_state: i = 1 (value 7): complement 6 misses; after insertion, map = {2: 0, 7: 1}.
frames.announcement: Visit element 7 at index 1; complement 6 is not in the hash table, so store key-value pair 7: 1 in map.

frames.title: Complement 2 found, return indices
frames.explanation: i = 2 points to element 11. As noted on the right of the figure, because 13 - 11 = 2 is already in map with map[2] = 0, return indices [0, 2]. map remains {2: 0, 7: 1}; 11 is not inserted, and 15 at index 3 is never processed.
frames.key_state: i = 2 (value 11): complement 2 hits index 0 in map, immediately returning [0, 2]. map remains {2: 0, 7: 1}, 11 is not inserted, and 15 is not processed.
frames.announcement: Visit element 11 at index 2, find complement 2 (index 0) in the hash table, and return [0, 2].
